articles.title: A Teen Scientist's Warning: Caffeine Could Quiet Crucial Brain Genes in Kids
articles.summary: Sophia Zeng, 16, found that caffeine may dial down genes vital for brain development in young animals. Her experiments with rat neurons and zebrafish showed fewer neural connections and more anxiety-like behavior. The effects appeared different in young versus adult brains, raising concerns about kids' caffeine habits.

articles.title: Battery-Free Solar Fuel: How a Self-Heating Device Turns Sunlight into Energy
articles.summary: Japanese researchers created an artificial photosynthesis system that produces formic acid from sunlight, water, and CO2 without batteries. A built-in solid electrolyte self-regulates by heating up, automatically optimizing power flow. The device worked outdoors and powered a diorama at the 2025 Osaka Expo.

articles.title: Not Just Mimics: Study Suggests Parrots Use Names Like Humans Do
articles.summary: Researchers analyzed recordings from over 880 captive parrots and found many use names as labels for specific individuals. Some birds even used their own name to seek attention. The study, published in PLOS ONE, hints at complex social communication skills in parrots.
